$comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the 2026 cyclosporiasis outbreak monitor. Updated by scripts/update-cyclosporiasis-monitor via scheduled task, then injected into the guide HTML by scripts/inject-outbreak-monitor.js at build time. Never hand-edit case numbers without a primary-source URL + verifiedDate. All regulatory/surveillance claims must trace to CDC or FDA.

sourceIdentified.product: Shredded iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms de Mexico (central Mexico) served at Taco Bell locations in Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, and West Virginia
sourceIdentified.confirmedBy: FDA & CDC epidemiologic and traceback data (advisory July 16–17, 2026; still active July 21)
sourceIdentified.basisNote: The link rests on epidemiologic and traceback evidence (how FDA usually identifies a source), not on a positive food test. CDC states this lettuce 'is contaminated with Cyclospora and is making people sick.'
sourceIdentified.falsePositiveNote: On July 18 the FDA reported a separate border-screening lettuce sample as positive; on July 19 lab experts re-reviewed it and called it a FALSE POSITIVE, and the FDA apologized to Taylor Farms for that lab error. FDA says this does NOT change the ongoing investigation or the recall, which remain in effect. As of July 19 there are no confirmed positive product samples.
sourceIdentified.recallStatus: Taylor Farms de Mexico's voluntary recall of central-Mexico iceberg lettuce (27 states) remains active; Taco Bell has stopped using the implicated supplier.
sourceIdentified.scopeNote: This 5-state Taco Bell cluster is a subset of the larger nationwide outbreak; other products may still be identified for remaining cases.

statesHardestHit.note: Largest cluster in state history (usual annual total is ~50). After 1,000+ patient interviews, MDHHS says lettuce/salad greens is a likely source, though no grower, brand, or product is confirmed.
Second-highest state count; includes New York City.
Part of a CDC-linked 4-state Midwest cluster (Michigan, Ohio, West Virginia, Kentucky).

linkedCluster.note: CDC has linked a multistate cluster of 400+ cases across four Midwestern states.

likelySource.product: Lettuce / salad greens (per Michigan MDHHS, not federally confirmed)

keyClinical.hallmark: watery, sometimes explosive diarrhea in a remitting-relapsing pattern lasting weeks if untreated
keyClinical.treatment: TMP-SMX (Bactrim/Septra) one double-strength tablet twice daily for 7–10 days
